limited_overlap.description: applicants with prior_earnings between 49,950 and 880,160: 91% of the 1800 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.
applicants whose follow-up earnings are not recorded: their effect is identified only if non-response is unrelated to earnings given the adjustment set and enrolment (1927 training applicants).

warnings: Enrolled and non-enrolled applicants differ in pre-enrolment columns: mean prior earnings 17,752 against 37,570; the estimates adjust for the columns listed under roles.
experience is an exact linear combination of the other pre-enrolment columns; it is not put in the adjustment set, and its information is carried by the columns it is built from.

No covariate passed the claim rule (joint p below 0.05 in the primary fit, at the median of four nuisance fits, with one sign). Candidates by median joint p: education p=0.0848 (+714, +871, +1049, +872 dollars per SD); region p=0.0851 (-1613, -1137, -1305, -1490 dollars per SD); age p=0.197 (+221, +1677, +748, +614 dollars per SD); ethnicity p=0.201 (-1942, -283, -1791, -1634 dollars per SD). The joint p-value of each covariate moved across fold splits (the single-split fit gave p near 0.004 for age and 0.03 for prior earnings), so no covariate is claimed as an effect modifier.
17.5% of training rows have a cross-fitted propensity outside the overlap bounds; the all-rows ATE depends on the outcome model in those rows, and the overlap-bounded estimate is 559 dollars.
Instrument check (distance_km, responders only): complier effect -2,421 dollars with 90% interval [-10,466, 5,624], against the ATE -433. The complier effect and the ATE are different quantities.
Certificate and hours worked are measured during or after the program and are mediators; they are not adjusted for, so the estimates are total effects that include the paths through them.

Test applicants differ from training applicants in means: prior_earnings 31,503.8 (train) against 25,877.0 (test); months_unemployed 2.7 (train) against 3.1 (test). Per-applicant effects for test applicants outside the training range are extrapolated.

Test applicants outside the propensity overlap bounds: 7.0%. 73 of the 800 applicants at the top of the cate order are among them; their effects come from the outcome model, not from comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants. Restricting the top group to the overlap region gives 800 applicants with mean cate 1,610 dollars.
Test applicants outside the training range of an effect-model term: 2.4%.

No covariate passed the modifier rule, so no effect modifier is claimed. The per-applicant effects and the ranking come from a model on the lead covariates ['education', 'region', 'age'], whose evidence is weak; the ranking carries less information than the interval widths suggest.
